narrative:
The model determined that you have a 27% chance of representing a bad credit risk. While this is not an extremely high probability, it was enough for the bank to deny your loan application.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this decision were the length of the loan you requested, your credit history, and the status of your checking account. The short six-month duration you asked for actually worked in your favor, as it is much shorter than the average of 19 months among approved applicants and pushed the prediction toward good credit. Your credit history marked as "critical or other credits" also helped your case, since this category is relatively common among approved loans and pulled the prediction away from bad credit.

Unfortunately, the status of your checking account proved to be the deciding factor. Your account being in negative balance (<0 DM) is fairly uncommon; only 12.6% of applicants are in this situation, while the majority (59%) have no checking account at all. This negative status strongly pushed the model toward classifying you as a bad credit risk, outweighing the positive effects of the shorter loan term and your credit history.

To improve your chances next time, focus on bringing your checking account balance into positive territory before reapplying. Consider requesting a longer loan if your finances allow, as shorter durations appear to be viewed more cautiously in some cases. You may also want to review your full credit report to ensure everything is accurate. (218 words)
